title: Development and validation of an interpretable Random Forest model for predicting recurrence after endoscopic submucosal dissection in superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Development and validation of an interpretable Random Forest model for predicting recurrence after endoscopic submucosal dissection in superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background · abstract-1-1】Currently, endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) has become the preferred treatment for superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma (SESCC). However, due to the residual background mucosa, some patients are still at risk of postoperative recurrence. This study aimed to develop and validate an explainable machine learning model to predict recurrence risk in SESCC patients undergoing ESD.

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Oesophageal cancer is a prevalent malignancy with high incidence and mortality rates worldwide [1]. The two main subtypes of oesophageal cancer are squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma, and there are marked geographical variations in their distribution. China has a high incidence of oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) [2]. Due to absence of typical symptoms in the early stages, many patients have entered the middle and late stages when diagnosed, leading to poor overall prognosis and a five-year survival rate of less than 30% [3]. Studies have shown that after endoscopic or surgical treatment of oesophageal cancer in the early stage, the five-year survival rate can reach 95% [4]. Therefore, improving the early diagnosis rate of oesophageal cancer and implementing timely treatment can contribute to improve patient prognosis. Superficial oesophageal squamous carcinoma (SESCC) refers to oesophageal cancer confined to the oesophageal mucosa or submucosa. In recent years, the popularization of endoscopic screening technology and the application of high-resolution imaging technologies have significantly improved the detection rate of SESCC, providing an important window period for minimally invasive treatment.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Development and validation of an interpretable Random Forest model for predicting recurrence after endoscopic submucosal dissection in superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Patients · S0002-S2001-p1】This study retrospectively collected patients with SESCC who received ESD treatment at the Endoscopy Center of the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University from 1 January 2016 to 31 December 2023. We included the patients with the following criteria: (1) Initial ESD treatment; (2) SESCC was confirmed by postoperative pathology; (3) Complete medical record information and endoscopic treatment data; (4) Follow-up time exceeded six months. The exclusion criteria were as follows: (1) Patients who were not undergoing ESD treatment for the first time; (2) Patients who underwent endoscopic surgery other than ESD for the first time; (3) Patients who had undergone surgical oesophagectomy or other anti-tumour therapies before or after ESD;(4) Patients with other malignancies were excluded; (5) Patients with incomplete clinical data or lost to follow-up after ESD. This retrospective study was approved by the Ethics Committee and Review Committee of the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University (2024-SR-499), and all patients provided written informed consent before receiving ESD treatment. The flow chart of this study is shown in Figure 1.

【Methods · abstract-2-1】We enrolled SESCC patients treated with ESD between 1 January 2016 and 31 December 2023. Patients from 2016 to 2021 were allocated to the training set, further split into a 7:3 ratio for model training and internal validation. Patients from 2022 to 2023 constituted the temporal validation set. Seven machine learning algorithms - logistic regression, extreme gradient boosting, light gradient boosting machine, random forest (RF), gradient boosting decision tree, Gaussian Naïve Bayes and Multilayer Perceptron - were employed to construct risk models. Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) method was applied to interpret the optimal model's feature importance.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Development and validation of an interpretable Random Forest model for predicting recurrence after endoscopic submucosal dissection in superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Model performance evaluation and interpretation · S0002-S2007-p1】The area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) served as the primary statistical criterion for selecting the best-performing machine learning model, while accuracy, sensitivity, positive predictive value (PPV), F1-score and the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) were used to comprehensively assess model performance. The closer these statistical metrics are to 1, the better the model’s predictive performance. The DeLong test was employed to determine whether there was a significant difference in the AUC values of different models [16]. Additionally, calibration curves were employed to evaluate how well the predicted probabilities aligned with the observed results. Decision curve analysis (DCA) was performed to effectively evaluate the clinical utility of the model in real-world decision-making. We employed the Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) approach to elucidate the predictive model, providing insight into the influence of individual variables on outcomes [17]. As a game theory-based method, SHAP enables interpretation at both the individual prediction level and the overall model level, improving transparency and interpretability [18]. To facilitate the application of the model by clinicians, researchers, patients and their families, the final predictive model was integrated into a web-based platform developed using the Shiny application. Users can obtain predictive results simply by entering relevant clinical parameters on the web interface.

【Model development and performance comparison · S0004-S2006-p1】The selected features were utilized for model training and validation. Performance evaluation on the internal test set (Figure 4) showed that all seven machine learning models (LR, XGBoost, LightGBM, RF, GBDT, GNB and MLP) exhibited strong discriminative ability, with AUC (95% CI) values of 0.666 (0.548–0.784), 0.865 (0.785–0.946), 0.747 (0.636–0.858), 0.892 (0.818–0.965), 0.855 (0.771–0.939), 0.688 (0.573–0.803) and 0.583 (0.459–0.707), respectively. Table 2 compares key performance metrics across the seven machine learning models. Based on the comprehensive performance evaluation, the RF model demonstrated superior predictive ability for recurrence risk, with the highest accuracy (0.823 [0.795–0.851]), specificity (0.948 [0.926–0.969]), positive predictive value (PPV) (0.914 [95% CI 0.879–0.949]) and F1-score (0.77 [95% CI 0.729–0.811]). Additionally, precision-recall curve analysis (Figure 4) demonstrated that the RF model achieved the highest area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) in the internal test set, reaching 0.905 (95% CI 0.883–0.927). The DeLong test showed that the AUC of the RF model was higher than that of several other models, and the differences were statistically significant (p < .05) (Supplementary Table S4). The calibration curve indicated that the RF model exhibited the highest calibration performance, with a calibration score of 0.125 (95% CI: 0.112–0.138). Decision curve analysis (DCA) indicated that the RF model outperformed all others across the full threshold range (0.2–0.8), with the XGBoost model ranking second. Overall, the RF model was identified as the optimal approach for risk prediction. To assess its generalizability, the trained RF model was temporally validated, yielding an AUC of 0.761 (95% CI: 0.659–0.863), confirming its robustness (Figure 5). Supplementary Table 5 shows the hyperparameters for the seven models.
